SEGMENT Il LANDOWNERS INITIAL BRIEF - PARTY NO. 471

COMES NOW Segment i1 Landowners (“Landowners”), Party No. 471 in SOAH Order No. 31, and files this Post Hearing Rebuttal Brief.
In sum, regarding the proposed route that best meets the applicable statutory and Commission requirements, Landowners support the recommendation of the two parties in this case that are the most qualified to conduct the required in-depth analysis for the process and the only parties disinterested in the location of the proposed facilities other than compliance with applicable standards: the Applicants, for Route 894, and Commission Staff, for Route 487. Landowners have shown that Route Segment i1 is unsuitable for use in a transmission line route and provided testimony admitted into evidence in the docket, Segment i1 Landowners Exhibits 1 and 2. 
Many parties have raised concerns about the environmental impact by Route 894. The direct testimony of Rae Lynn Schneider Reinecke on behalf of Cherokee Creek Partners suggests Route CCG is environmentally better, but it is important to remember that there must be balance in this evaluation. Environmental factors are only one of the many considerations for selecting a route. Further, Applicants expert witness, Corin E Cooley, testified Applicant has techniques and strategies for addressing environmental issues that arise. Ms. Cooley also explained that cost estimates have been included in the Application for addressing any sensitive environmental areas. That being said, Route 894 is one of the strongest performing routes with respect to environmental integrity. It includes only 291 stream crossings, has only 1.97 miles of potential wetlands, second lowest among the Routes of Interest, Intervenor proposed routes, and crosses only 42.52 miles of riparian areas, which is lower than other Routes of Interest. Route 894 crosses no park or recreational area, and has no park or recreational area within 1,000 feet. On matters of environmental sensitivity, Route 894 is among the best performing routes compared with the other Routes of Interest.
Additional factors that the Commission looks for in a Route, Total Project Cost and Habitable Structure, shows Route 894 outperforming other Routes of Interest. For example, Route CCG, suggested by Cherokee Creek Partners and Ms. Reinecke, performs inferiorly with both cost and habitable structures in comparison to Route 894. In fact, Ms. Reinecke testified that her analyses were unconcerned about project costs.  Route CCG cost $74 million more to construct and has an additional 20 more habitable structures than Route 894. Route 572, proposed by Save The Lampasas (Party 391), cost an additional $8.33 million more than the Applicants “best meets” Route 894. Route 572 is also longer, impacts 22 more habitable structures, impacts more rangeland pastures and wetlands. It requires 45 more stream crossings and impacts more lakes and ponds as compared to Route 894.
Historical, archaeological and cultural sites have been front and center in the hearings on merit as Texans look to protect the history of their lands while working with The Texas Historical Commission. A recommendation of Route 296 by Jerome and Gaylynn Sneed fails to show that PUC Staff Engineer John Poole testified he had not been aware of a trinomial on Segment G6 when he evaluated Route 296. Upon learning of this fact, he agreed that information would make Route 296 “even more inferior” to the route he recommended, 487.  Significant historical, archaeological and cultural sites recorded with trinomials on Segments G6 and Segment i1 make the use of both routes unsuitable for transmission line projects. Route 894 has only 12 recorded cultural resources within 1,000 feet of the route centerline, while Route 572 would cross three cultural sites and have 19 nearby cultural resources. CCG would cross two sites but would have 18 recorded cultural resources within 1,000 feet of the route centerline, which is 50% more than Route 894. Further, Route 894 also has 54.34 miles of high archeological/historical site potential, materially lower than Route 572 at 64.15 miles and CCG at 62.79 miles.
During Mr. Poole’s cross examination at the hearings on merit, information presented had not been taken into account when considering the routing of 296. Upon consideration and in light of the new information presented, Route 296 was, in Mr. Poole’s judgement, an inferior route to 487. Additionally, Florence, Texas has a newly constructed elementary school which showed as a commercial industrial site vs school location for the Applicant. The transmission line will come within 450 feet of the school building but even closer to the playground. Mr. Poole was not aware of the Florence Elementary school.  Mr. Poole testified that had he been aware of an elementary school it “would have affected [his prior] recommendation.”    Mr. Poole also noted “schools are important to avoid.”
As explained by Applicants' witness Casey D. Petty, the Applicant initially identified 1,246 potential routes for the transmission line. From this large number of options, Applicants' analyses narrowed the options down to 122 routes as the most potentially compliant with state statutory standards and Commission rules. Intervenors presenting and advocating for a particular route, do so as to not have a transmission line located on or near their property. This is certainly an understandable motivation for engagement in the hearing on merit. However, the process of route selection must comply with the requirements and standards set forth in the Public Utility Regulatory Act ("PURA") and Commission's rules. 
	Ms. Petty testified that her selection of Route 894 was based on PURA § 37.056(c)(4)(A) -(D) and 16 TAC § 25.101, including prudent avoidance, environmental assessment, cost, engineering analysis, and personal reconnaissance of the study area. As well, LCRA TSC witness Kelly Wells confirmed that LCRA TSC supports Route 894 as the route that addresses the requirements of PURA and the Commission’s Substantive Rules.
	Mr. John Poole, the Commission Staff expert witness, provided independent analyses free from any routing preferences. Mr. Poole is an experienced engineer who has testified in 38 transmission CCN cases. Based on his review of the Applicants information, the Environmental Assessment, testimony and evidence provided by all parties of the docket, his recommendation is Route 487. After the Hearing on Merits which proved additional information from cross examination, Mr. Poole did not change his recommendation regarding the best route.
From direct testimony and through the hearings on merits, several alternative routes by different intervenors have been suggested in order to divert the transmission lines away from their respective properties. This is understandable but the alternative routes suggested have significant drawbacks and fail to overcome the superior character of Route 894 and 487 in meeting the applicable standards. Furthermore, during cross examination many intervenors tried to undermine the recommendations of the Applicants’ witness and the Commissions’ Mr. Poole. These intervenors failed to prove that Route 894 and Route 487 are inferior to any alternative route suggestion as well as to sway the Applicant or Mr. Poole into changing their recommendations in support of Route 894 and Route 487.
Landowners appreciate the professional approach the State Office of Administration Hearings (“SOAH”) Admiration Law Judges (“ALJs”) employed during the hearing on merits. Landowners greatly appreciate the help and consideration given to pro se intervenors who, like a majority of the landowners, have not been through a proceeding of this type. Many parties have agreed that the ALJ’s efficiency in addressing issues, making rulings with clarity and keeping forward progress made the hearing efficient. 
Segment i1 Landowners urge that, if the proposed 765 kv transmission project is to be approved, the ALJ’s issue a Proposal for Decision recommending Route 894 or Route 487. It is our belief that the proposed Route 894 and Route 487 best meets the requirements of state law and Commission standards. Landowners urge the ALJ’s not recommend any transmission lines routes that include Route Segment i1, for the reasons set forth in the record in this case.

						Respectfully submitted,		
						/s/ Marylynne Norman
						Marylynne G. Norman
						President, Segment i1 Landowners
						Party 471
						On behalf of all members of
